committed: Before the two ring scenarios, the instruments or the three investigations existed, and before any engine run of either scenario was inspected. The only numbers looked at beforehand were a collisionless test-particle probe (planet, one resonant moon, 800 massless particles) used to choose how heavy the schematic resonant moon must be; its output is not an oracle and is not quoted here. A leg that fails is recorded and reported with its cause and the bound is not moved.
scope: Part 2 builds what verdict B of TIDAL_TORQUE_GATE.md leaves: the displays. No engine torque, no extra force, no integrator change: both scenarios are plain Newtonian N-body worlds built from the geometry table, so the checks below are about the declarations and about what an unmodified engine does with them, over a fixed run at a fixed seed.

ring-gap.what: A ringed planet at the scale of Saturn and Mimas (true mass of the planet, lengths in a scale model, G carrying the exaggeration as the Earth-Moon System does), a ring of massless-for-practical-purposes particles across the radius where a moon's 2:1 resonance falls, a resonant moon at the Mimas distance with an exaggerated mass (stated), a shepherd moon just outside the ring.

s1.resonance.radius.what: the declared ring contains the 2:1 radius a_m (1/2)^(2/3) and the engine's resonant moon is at the declared distance; the radius equals the tides kernel's resonanceRadius to 1e-12

s2.eccentricity.what: mean osculating eccentricity of ring particles within the window about the 2:1 radius after the run, divided by the mean over the flanks (2 to 4 window half-widths either side)

s3.thinning.what: particles inside the window about the 2:1 radius after the run, divided by the mean of the two flanks. A collisionless ring thins at a resonance and does not empty: reported honestly and held to a modest bound

s4.shepherd.what: the share of ring particles beyond (ring outer edge minus 0.03 moon orbits) after the run, divided by the same share at the start: the shepherd's chaotic zone removes the ring's outermost particles and leaves a sharp edge

s5.control.what: the same planet and ring with no moon: after the same run the window ratio stays at least 0.85 and the mean eccentricity in the window stays below 0.01 (the ring is stable by itself, so s2 to s4 are the moons' doing)

s6.bodies.what: at least 90 percent of the ring particles remain alive and every position is finite after the run

revision.what: Added after s4 was measured and failed, before the engine was run on the revised design. The design first built put the shepherd outside the ring (78 units, ratio 3e-5, and in two variants 1e-4): the share beyond the cutoff rose from 25 to 29 or 34 particles (ratio 1.16 to 1.36 against the committed 0.5) because the scattered particles are excited, not removed, so s4 FAILED as committed and stays failed in the record. A collisionless ring does not keep a sharp edge against a moon outside it in twenty orbits. The shepherd was moved inside the ring (72 units), which is where Pan and Daphnis act, and the leg below is what a moonlet in a ring does by the Hill-radius argument; a plain test-particle probe at the same masses put the lane count at about half its starting value, and the bound is set at 0.6.

s4b.lane.what: particles whose orbital radius is 2 to 4 Hill radii from the shepherd's orbit (either side; Hill radius a (m / 3M)^(1/3) of the shepherd) after the run, divided by the same count at the start

roche-pass.what: A planet and a clump of bound particles (a rubble pile) on an orbit whose periapsis is inside the planet's fluid Roche limit for the clump's density, after Shoemaker-Levy 9 (1.3 Jupiter radii against a fluid limit of 3.2 and a rigid limit of 1.6).

r1.limits.what: the declared periapsis is inside the kernel's rigid limit and the fluid limit (2.44 and the exact 2.4553) for the densities the declared masses and radii give; the rigid coefficient is 2^(1/3)

r2.stretch.what: after periapsis the clump's largest extent divided by its starting extent

r3.control.what: the same clump with the periapsis at 1.5 times the fluid limit, run as long: its extent after the pass divided by its starting extent stays under 2

r4.bodies.what: no particle is lost to contact with the planet in the disrupting pass (at least 90 percent alive) and every position is finite

lessonNumbers.what: Every number a step states is recomputed in tests/tidesLessons.test.js from the kernel (js/kernels/tides/) and compared to the step's stated value at the tolerance written in the step; a step may state a number only if the test names it.
